concepts.definition: SourceVersion/2 is the complete managed/external production-version union: both arms bind full EntityRef, production CommitDomain, and production observationEpoch; managed additionally binds the checked H(D,E)+1 revision and seal ChangeId, while external binds externalSequence and has no managed revision/ChangeId. Current observation remains separately represented by SourceObservation/1 and SourceVersionRef/1. The new d6_source_revision/2 profile is a stable production address: RevisionTokenBinding/2 contains token plus RevisionTokenSource/2 only. Before C/Q materialization the original plan freezes one proposed binding; the winning P seal creates the actual managed SourceVersion and, in that same transaction, creates RevisionTokenSealAssociation/1 and domain-separated Ed25519 RevisionTokenSealArtifact/1, pins its exact D3-CJ/3 canonical bytes as portable metadata, and records RevisionTokenSealOutboxItem/1. RevisionTokenSealVerificationKey/1 is the protected normalized view of the already-authenticated historical shared trust declaration for the producing CommitDomain/profile at the seal cut. Receiver admission verifies CP3/history and the signed artifact independently and cross-checks DecisionKey, ChangeId, complete SourceVersion and SourceStamp fields before storing token→production-version mapping. CP3/Notice shapes do not gain the binding or artifact.
concepts.exclusions: Not a bare revision, digest, path, DocumentRef, currentness proof, permission, writable selector, ActionEvidence, Draft/PAB/PreparedIntent capability, sender attestation, or replacement for SourceObservation/1. Equal revision/stamp/version/hash/bytes cannot authenticate a token without the original signed artifact and historical trust key. A loser/aborted/unproved token has no valid artifact; publication, retry and I rebuild never reconstruct or re-sign one. External equal bytes do not inherit an event/token. Two non-byte-equal artifacts for one exact managed SourceVersion are an integrity contradiction only when both independently validate from the historical portable-trust root.

concepts.exampleAndCounterexample: A seals V with t and one signed RevisionTokenSealArtifact/1; B verifies the historical trust declaration, signature, association and CP3 V, then creates its own current SourceObservation and reads the unchanged Locator. A same-stamp forged t2 without a valid signature is unavailable, not a conflict. If two distinct artifacts for the same exact V both validate from the historical trust root, that is an integrity contradiction. Real production ABA, missing artifact/trust history, loser/aborted plans, or equal-byte external observation never fabricate qualification.

concepts.definition: DependencyProof/2 binds Workspace/CommitDomain/base Frontier to complete positive/negative evidence over exactly fourteen closed DependencyKey/2 kinds—source, lifecycle, placement_range, ref_inbound, relation_incidence, calendar_scope, registry, temporal_rules, authorization, foreign_binding, query_scan, replica_registry, conflict_record, execution_resource—with owner-defined complete ranges, evidence pins, and per-key continuity stamp {epoch,revision}. Completeness comes from a currently authorized consistent snapshot/range barrier or a gap-free continuous change chain plus final revalidation; D6 carries the closed keys/stamps while D3/D4/D7 retain their actual enumeration algorithms. Only the guarded D3 resolution context may bind a source entry to the complete typed ConflictInstallInput/1 plus conflict/current-range evidence; it proves that original installation and never exports canonical-current Query qualification.
concepts.exclusions: Not caller readSet/free JSON, Derived Index readiness, row count, final hash, provider-synced status, Frontier-vector comparison, partial/building index, unknown range, or no-hit evidence. Deleting I alone does not reset proof while protected P/M continuity facts remain complete; actual proof/continuity loss or a gap requires a new epoch.

concepts.definition: ConflictRecord/2 is the current new-FA portable conflict record addressed by the unchanged canonical ConflictKey/1 and ConflictId, with createdAtFrontier encoded as Frontier/2 and state open|resolution_prepared|resolved|superseded. ConflictKey/1 ordering, ConflictId format, and the D6-ConflictKey/1 hash domain are unchanged. Historical ConflictRecord/1 retains its original bytes, decoder, authorization/recovery obligations, and createdAtFrontier=Frontier/1. Current ConflictResolution/1 contains only source_merge, choose_source_head and policy_choice, which D6 can actually prepare. The undeployed owner_resolution candidate arm is removed. Clients navigate placement/lifecycle/identity conflicts directly to D3ConflictResolutionPrepare/1 in D3 §10.1; final submission retains identity_operation_request wire12 with its actual preparationBinding and the same DecisionKey/P decision. D3 owns complete typed selection, three-entity selected-branch copy and native resolution consumption. D7 owns the actual PreparedActionBinding/3 record and full EffectManifest/2/current preview transport; their coordinated producer and independent acceptance remain required before new prepared execution. Resolution input requires its immutable preparationBinding/input-use guard and cannot become raw input by stripping a token; real saved/planned/unknown records recover first under their original contract.
concepts.exclusions: Not automatic merge, LWW, D3 bypass transaction, permission, or a reason to reinterpret Record/1 as Record/2. An external race, third_state, or unknown installation with no real sealed ChangeId cannot fabricate a ConflictKey head; equal hash/mtime/path is not conflict-history evidence. No permanent route-only failing RPC, free payload, new D6 route-success result, second D6 identity submit or second ledger. Removal of an undeployed candidate arm does not assert deployment or cancel the original decoder/pin/recovery duties of any historical record that actually exists.
